templates.name: Fire Alarm (NFPA 72)
templates.title: FIRE ALARM SYSTEM
sub: In Accordance with NFPA 72 — National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code

sections.t: A. PANEL & POWER SUPPLY INSPECTION [NFPA 72: 14.3.1, 10.5]

items.t: Inspect panel enclosure & all field wiring cables — check for physical damage, corrosion, loose terminations; report deficiencies immediately
Open panel — inspect PCBs, power supply unit; verify no burn marks, corrosion, or damaged components
Verify AC mains supply voltage (nominal 220 V); record panel voltage: _______ V
Clean panel interior & PCBs with soft anti-static brush to remove dust accumulation
Confirm all field cables are securely terminated on terminal blocks; tighten any loose connections

sections.t: B. BATTERY INSPECTION & TESTING [NFPA 72: 10.5.9, 14.4.3]

items.t: Measure and record standby battery voltages: B1: _______ V    B2: _______ V
Clean battery terminals with dry cloth; remove any oxidation
Inspect battery terminals for corrosion — if corroded, advise client for immediate replacement
Check battery charge voltage (must be ≥27 V DC); if low, adjust charger or replace battery
Perform battery backup test: disconnect AC mains and confirm system operates on battery for minimum 10 minutes (verify 24-hr standby + 5-min alarm capacity per design)
Restore AC mains supply after battery test; confirm charger resumes and panel returns to normal supervisory state

sections.t: C. DETECTOR TESTING [NFPA 72: 14.4.4, 14.4.5]

items.t: Test smoke detectors using listed aerosol spray (simulate smoke) — record loop/detector no. & location for each tested device:
Test heat detectors using appropriate thermal test method — verify correct alarm activation and FACP indication
During detector test: confirm all alarm notification appliances (sounders, speakers, flashers) activate and FACP displays correct zone/device information
Clean all dirty/dusty detectors with approved cleaning method; replace any detector exceeding manufacturer's sensitivity limits

sections.t: D. NOTIFICATION APPLIANCES [NFPA 72: 14.4.8]

items.t: Test all audible sounders — activate alarm and verify sufficient sound levels throughout the protected area
Test all voice/alarm speakers — activate alarm or conduct fire drill; confirm intelligible audio in all zones
Test all visual (strobe/flasher) appliances — activate alarm or fire drill; verify correct flash rate and coverage

sections.t: E. SYSTEM INTEGRITY & COMPLIANCE [NFPA 72: 14.3.2, 4.4]

items.t: Check monitoring of supervisory signals (AC fail, battery fault, ground fault, open circuit) — verify all fault signals annunciate correctly
Verify panel event log/history is accessible and up to date; record last fault events if any
During inspection: any device found faulty/damaged — record details and inform client representative immediately
Affix updated maintenance sticker on FACP (include service date, technician name, next due date)
Confirm all opened/removed devices are reinstated and panel is in full normal supervisory state at job completion

templates.foot: This checklist is following NFPA 72 (Current Edition) — National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code. Retain for minimum 3 years per

templates.name: FM-200 Clean Agent (NFPA 2001)
templates.title: FM200 FIRE SUPPRESSION SYSTEM
sub: In Accordance with NFPA 2001 (Clean Agent) & NFPA 72 (Fire Alarm & Signaling Code)

sections.t: A. CONTROL PANEL & POWER SUPPLY [NFPA 2001: 7.3 | NFPA 72: 10.5]

items.t: Inspect suppression control panel enclosure check for physical damage, corrosion, error/fault indicators; record any active faults
Verify AC mains supply voltage is 220 V; record actual reading: _______ V
Measure and record standby battery voltages:       B1: _______ V    B2: _______ V
Inspect battery terminals for corrosion; clean terminals and tighten connections; advise client for replacement if corrosion is excessive
Perform 10-minute battery backup test — disconnect AC mains, confirm system operates normally on battery standby
Restore AC mains; confirm charger resumes, panel returns to normal supervisory state, no residual faults
Clean control panel interior, PCBs, and field cables using soft anti-static brush; ensure no dust accumulation on boards

sections.t: B. CYLINDER, AGENT & DISTRIBUTION [NFPA 2001: 7.4, 7.5]

items.t: Check FM200 (HFC-227ea) cylinder pressure gauge  confirm pressure is within manufacturer's specified normal range: _______ Bar
Inspect cylinder for physical damage, corrosion, or signs of leakage; verify cylinder mounting brackets are secure
Inspect all discharge nozzles confirm nozzles are unobstructed, correctly oriented, and free from damage or paint overspray
Inspect all pipes work and fittings for corrosion, mechanical damage, or unauthorized modification; confirm pipe supports are intact
Confirm solenoid valve is properly connected to cylinder and in armed (normal) position; tag shall be in place

sections.t: C. MANUAL DEVICES & ABORT STATION [NFPA 2001: 7.6]

items.t: Inspect Manual Release Station verify handle/button is accessible, unobstructed, correctly labelled, and in normal (armed) position
Inspect Abort Switch verify condition, accessibility, correct labelling, and operational readiness; confirm it returns to normal after test

sections.t: D. DETECTION SYSTEM (CROSS-ZONE / DUAL DETECTOR LOGIC) [NFPA 72: 14.4.4 | NFPA 2001: 7.2]

items.t: Functionally test all smoke/heat detectors in the protected hazard zone using approved test method; verify correct response and FACP indication
Clean all detectors after testing using approved cleaning method; confirm each device returns to normal supervisory state
Verify system wiring network continuity  check for open circuits, grounds, or short circuits on detection loops

sections.t: E. FUNCTIONAL SYSTEM TEST PROCEDURE · E1 — Pre-Test Safety Preparation [NFPA 2001: 7.7.1]

items.t: Notify all responsible persons and occupants in the affected area prior to commencing functional test
Disconnect FM200 panel interface from FACP (if interfaced) to prevent false discharge signal to other systems
Disconnect solenoid valve actuator from cylinder head to prevent accidental agent discharge during functional test

sections.t: E. FUNCTIONAL SYSTEM TEST PROCEDURE · E2 — First Stage Activation (Alert) [NFPA 2001: 7.7.4]

items.t: Activate one detector in the protected hazard area (cross-zone first stage); confirm detector responds correctly
Verify audible bell/alert sounder activates on first stage alarm signal
Confirm fire suppression panel annunciates first stage alarm with correct zone/device information

sections.t: E. FUNCTIONAL SYSTEM TEST PROCEDURE · E3 — Second Stage Activation (Discharge Sequence) [NFPA 2001: 7.7.5]

items.t: Activate second detector in the same protected zone (cross-zone second stage); confirm detector responds correctly
Verify sounder with flasher (visual/audible notification) activates on second stage signal
Confirm panel annunciates second stage alarm and initiates countdown timer for agent release
Verify countdown timer delay is correctly programmed: _______ sec (design basis: 30 sec minimum per NFPA 2001)

sections.t: E. FUNCTIONAL SYSTEM TEST PROCEDURE · E4 — Programming & Panel Functions [NFPA 2001: 7.7.6]

items.t: Test Silence Alarm button — verify it silences audible notification while maintaining alarm indication on panel
Test Abort Switch function — verify it correctly interrupts the countdown/discharge sequence when activated
Press Reset button — confirm panel resets to normal supervisory state with no residual faults or alarms

sections.t: F. SYSTEM RESTORATION & FINAL CHECKS [NFPA 2001: 7.7.7 | NFPA 72: 14.3.1]

items.t: Reconnect solenoid valve actuator to cylinder head; confirm connection is secure and cylinder valve is in armed position
Reconnect FM200 panel interface to FACP; verify all interface signals function correctly
Verify complete system is in normal operational condition — all indicators green, no errors, detector status normal
Affix updated maintenance sticker on suppression panel (service date, technician name, next scheduled service date)
Any deficiency found during inspection — record in Findings Log below and inform client representative immediately

templates.foot: This checklist is prepared in compliance with NFPA 2001 (Standard on Clean Agent Fire Extinguishing Systems) & NFPA 72 (National Fire Alarm and Signaling Code) — Current Editions. Records shall be retained for a minimum of 3 years per NFPA 2001: 7.3.3.

templates.name: Fire Pump (NFPA 25)
templates.title: FIRE PROTECTION SYSTEM — FIRE PUMP
sub: In Accordance with NFPA 25 (ITM of Water-Based Fire Protection Systems) & NFPA 72

sections.t: A. WATER SUPPLY, PIPING & DISTRIBUTION SYSTEM [NFPA 25: 4.1, 9.2]

items.t: Inspect fire water storage tank condition — verify tank is filled to required design level; check for structural damage, corrosion, or debris inside tank
Verify suction, discharge, and bypass valves are fully open and in correct normal operating position; confirm supervisory devices (tamper switches) are functional
Inspect all exposed piping, fittings, and supports for leaks, corrosion, mechanical damage, or unauthorized modification; confirm all pipe supports are intact
Check suction and system pressure gauges — verify readings are within design operating range; replace any gauge showing inaccurate or no reading
Confirm all control valves are accessible and  normal open position;
Inspect test line flow meter — verify flow meter is operational, , and test line valve operates correctly
Verify fire pump system is correctly interfaced with fire alarm system — confirm alarm/fault signals transmit to FACP as designed
Test & drain valve — open and verify correct flow; confirm valve closes fully and seats properly with no residual drip
Inspect sprinkler heads, pipes, fittings, hose boxes, and valves for physical damage, obstruction, and correct orientation
Test fire hose reels — unwind fully, verify hose is free from obstruction and kinks, nozzle operates correctly; confirm hose cabinet is accessible and labelled
Inspect Fire Department Connections (FDC/Siamese) — verify caps in place, threads undamaged, check valve operational, and FDC location is clearly marked and unobstructed

sections.t: B. ELECTRIC FIRE PUMP — DUTY PUMP INSPECTION · B1 — Controller & Electrical Supply [NFPA 25: 8.1.2]

items.t: Inspect fire pump control panel and field cables — check for physical damage, insulation deterioration, loose terminations; report deficiencies immediately
Clean control panel interior and PCB with soft anti-static brush; remove dust accumulation from components and terminal blocks
Confirm all field cables are firmly terminated on terminal blocks; tighten any loose connections
Check 3-phase supply voltage to pump — record each phase: Red: _______ V    Blue: _______ V    Yellow: _______ V (tolerance: ±10% of nominal)

sections.t: B. ELECTRIC FIRE PUMP — DUTY PUMP INSPECTION · B2 — Automatic & Manual Pump Operation Test [NFPA 25: 8.3.3]

items.t: Test automatic start — open test valve to simulate system pressure drop; confirm duty pump starts automatically at design cut-in pressure. Record: Cut-in: _______ PSI/Bar    Cut-off: _______ PSI/Bar
Perform manual operation test — run duty pump for minimum 10 minutes
Check for any abnormal sounds (cavitation, bearing noise, impeller noise) from motor or pump during operation
Inspect pump gland (mechanical seal or packing) — verify minor permitted weep; tighten gland follower if excessive leakage; replace packing if worn
Lubricate motor bearings with manufacturer-specified grease

sections.t: C. DIESEL ENGINE FIRE PUMP — STANDBY PUMP INSPECTION · C1 — Pre-Start Checks [NFPA 25: 8.2.2]

items.t: Check diesel fuel tank level — must be minimum two-thirds (2/3) full; top up if below minimum; inspect fuel lines for leaks
Confirm controller selector switch is in AUTO position; verify no override or manual hold-out condition is active

Measure and record battery voltages —
 B1: _____B2____ V DC; verify battery charger is on and charging voltage is correct
Check battery indicator lights — confirm charge indicators are ON; confirm failure/fault indicators are OFF
Verify all alarm indicators are OFF / in normal state before starting test
Check crankcase oil level — verify at FULL mark on dipstick; top up with manufacturer-specified oil grade if required
Check engine cooling water level in radiator/header tank — verify full; inspect for coolant leaks at hose connections; check coolant condition
Inspect battery terminals for corrosion — clean with appropriate solution and apply terminal protectant; confirm all connections are tight

sections.t: C. DIESEL ENGINE FIRE PUMP — STANDBY PUMP INSPECTION · C2 — Automatic & Manual Operation Test [NFPA 25: 8.3.3]

items.t: Test automatic start — release system pressure via test valve; confirm standby diesel pump starts automatically at design cut-in pressure. Record: Cut-in: _______ PSI/Bar    Cut-off: _______ PSI/Bar
Perform manual operation test — run diesel pump for minimum 10 minutes; monitor and record discharge pressure, RPM, coolant temp, oil pressure throughout run

sections.t: D. JOCKEY (PRESSURE MAINTENANCE) PUMP INSPECTION [NFPA 25: 8.1, 8.3.4]

items.t: Inspect jockey pump control panel and field cables — check for physical damage, loose terminations; report deficiencies immediately
Clean jockey pump control panel interior and PCB with soft anti-static brush
Confirm all field cables are firmly terminated on terminal blocks; tighten any loose connections
Check 3-phase supply voltage to jockey pump: Red: _______ V    Blue: _______ V    Yellow: _______ V

Test automatic operation — open test valve to drop system pressure; confirm jockey pump starts at design cut-in pressure and stops at cut-off. Record: Cut-in: _______ PSI/Bar    Cut-off: _______ PSI/Bar
Perform manual operation test — run jockey pump for minimum 10 minutes; verify discharge pressure is stable; monitor for abnormal noise or vibration
Check for abnormal sounds (bearing noise, cavitation) from jockey pump motor during operation
Inspect pump gland — verify no excessive leakage; tighten gland follower if required

sections.t: E. SYSTEM RESTORATION & FINAL VERIFICATION [NFPA 25: 4.1.3]

items.t: Confirm all valves are returned to their correct normal operating position after testing; re-seal or re-lock as required
Verify all three pump controllers (duty, standby, jockey) are set to AUTO and showing normal supervisory status with no active faults
Confirm fire pump system interface with FACP is restored and transmitting correct status signals; verify no residual fault indications
Review and record all system readings in this checklist; document any deficiencies in Findings Log and notify client representative
Affix updated maintenance sticker on each pump controller panel (service date, technician name, next scheduled service date)

templates.foot: This checklist is prepared in compliance with NFPA 25 (Standard for the Inspection, Testing, and Maintenance of Water-Based Fire Protection Systems) & NFPA 72 — Current Editions. Records shall be retained for a minimum of 3 years per NFPA 25: 4.1.3.
